methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: AI Ready Roanoke evaluates use for new technology in Roanoke Valley - Roanoke Times
signals.signal_reading: A civic initiative explicitly evaluating AI readiness in Roanoke Valley signals intentional capability-building in a non-metro region, but outcomes will determine whether this develops deep distributed capacity or remains concentrated in Virginia Tech's orbit.

signals.title: Virginia governor orders statewide plan to address AI cyberattacks - StateScoop
signals.signal_reading: A governor-ordered statewide AI cybersecurity plan suggests defensive platform adoption across state agencies—broad distribution but likely shallow implementation focused on vendor solutions rather than indigenous capability development.

signals.title: Norfolk, Newport News police launch AI tool for non-emergency calls - 13newsnow.com
signals.signal_reading: Norfolk and Newport News deploying AI tools for non-emergency calls demonstrates municipal-level platform adoption in Hampton Roads, signaling shallow but distributed implementation through vendor procurement rather than local AI development capacity.

signals.title: Amazon bows to local backlash over AI data centers, scraps plans to build four new facilities in Northern Virginia — site to be repurposed for mixed-use and residential development. - Tom's Hardware
signals.signal_reading: Amazon scrapping four NoVA data centers due to local backlash reveals community resistance to AI infrastructure concentration, potentially constraining even the region's deepest market advantage while other Virginia regions lack alternatives to fill the capability gap.

signals.title: Virginia Beach School Board to discuss AI use and student literacy data - 13newsnow.com
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Beach School Board discussing AI use and literacy signals education-sector platform adoption, pointing toward shallow distributed adoption through edtech vendors rather than building indigenous AI capability in students or educators.
